question.body:
A particle moves on the curve $y = x^3 - 3x$. Its $x$-coordinate satisfies $dif x / dif t = 1 / sqrt(2t + 1)$ for $t >= 0$, with $x(0) = -4$.

(a) Find $x(t)$.

(b) Find $dif y / dif t$ in terms of $t$.

(c) Find the location and speed of the particle at $t = 4$.
question.solution:
(a)
$ x(t) = integral 1 / sqrt(2t + 1) dif t = sqrt(2t + 1) + C. $
Using $x(0) = -4$ gives $C = -5$, so
$ x(t) = sqrt(2t + 1) - 5. $

(b) Since $y = x^3 - 3x$,
$ dif y / dif t = (3x^2 - 3) dif x / dif t. $
Therefore
$ dif y / dif t = (3(sqrt(2t + 1) - 5)^2 - 3) / sqrt(2t + 1). $

(c) $x(4) = 3 - 5 = -2$ and $y(4) = (-2)^3 - 3(-2) = -2$, so the location is $(-2, -2)$.

$ (dif x / dif t)|_(t=4) = frac(1, 3) $ and $ (dif y / dif t)|_(t=4) = 3$. Hence the speed is
$ sqrt((frac(1, 3))^2 + 3^2) = sqrt(frac(82, 9)) = frac(sqrt(82), 3) approx 3.018. $
